cues.en: Now in this video, we are going to learn how linked lists are stored in memory.

And this makes the accessibility of the arrays very easier and efficient.
Okay.
Let's see how the linked list is represented in memory.
So here we have a linked list in which we have four nodes.
So the first node is one and the second node is two which is referenced by one.
And the third node is four which is referenced by two, and the fourth node is five, which is referenced
by four.
So if you look at the memory how they are located in the memory, these nodes, we can easily see that
these nodes are not located contiguously.
So here the first node is referenced by head and the last node is referenced by tail.
And when we look at the next to the first node we see that it's empty.
So because the second node is located in a different place, we can only access it from the first node
by using the reference.
So in the first node we have a reference to the second node.
From the second node we have reference to the third node, and from the third node we have reference
to the fourth node.
So here a location is randomly.

nodes.

Each node needs an extra memory space for a pointer is required to link the nodes.

Because the size of the linked list does not need to be specified at the time of declaration, it allows
us dynamic resizing at runtime.
Because of random location of the elements in the memory, we cannot access any element directly due
to the fact that we don't know the location of any element.
We have to traverse from the first element to find the required element required element.
So, for example, if we want to access the third element over here, first we have to go to the first
element by using the head reference.
So in the head we have reference to the first node.
Then from first node we have a reference to the second node.
So we have to go to from first node to the second node.
Then from second node we have reference to the third node.
So we can go to the third node by using second node over here.
So this means that we cannot directly access this node over here.
But in case of array we always know the location of the elements with its index.

the third element is two.
So by using array name and inside square brackets we put to two.
We can access directly the third element in the memory because they are located contiguously.
So that's why we can easily identify the location of cell in case of array.
But in case of linked list, we cannot identify the location of the node until we start from the first
node and go to the that node using the next pointers of the nodes that we have in our memory.
